title: Lettuce Salad with Avocado, Tomato, and Carrots

content.title: About
content.content: The “Lettuce” salad is a mix of leafy lettuce, ripe avocado, fresh tomato, and grated carrot. Other vegetables may be added optionally, but no dressing is used, preserving the natural flavors of the ingredients.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Leafy lettuce is high in water content, helping to keep the body hydrated.
Avocado provides monounsaturated fats that are heart‑healthy.
Tomatoes are a rich source of lycopene, a powerful antioxidant.
Carrots are loaded with beta‑carotene, which the body converts to vitamin A.
The lack of dressing makes the salad low‑calorie and suitable for diet plans.

items.title: Supports Vision
items.content: Beta‑carotene from carrots and vitamin A promote eye health.

items.title: Heart Health
items.content: Monounsaturated fats in avocado help lower LDL cholesterol.

items.title: Antioxidant Protection
items.content: Lycopene from tomatoes and vitamin E from lettuce protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Hydration and Fiber
items.content: High water and fiber content aid digestion and increase satiety.

items.title: Immune Support
items.content: Vitamins C and K present in the salad strengthen the immune system.

items.title: Avocado Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to avocado.

items.title: Pesticide Residues
items.content: If the vegetables are not organic, pesticide residues may be present; thorough washing is recommended.

items.title: Digestive Discomfort
items.content: Large amounts of raw vegetables can cause gas in sensitive people.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the salad fresh as a standalone dish or as a side. Optionally add a squeeze of lemon, a pinch of salt, or your favorite herbs for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared salad in an airtight container in the refrigerator for no more than 24 hours to maintain crispness.
